title: Top 10 Women's College Basketball Players to Collect in 2026
meta_description: JuJu Watkins leads 10 college players to collect in 2026, with dated SportsCardsPro sales.
summary: A collecting list of ten college players, each tied to one card and, where a checklist has one, a completed SportsCardsPro sale with a date. The quick board sits under the intro, and the sales table only uses single-price rows.

uniqueness.summary: The dated sale table matches each listing title to the card in the photo, including parallels that share a checklist page.
points: Completed sales with a date, a single price, and the listing title
Joyce Edwards card-81 URL versus a #80 page with zero sold listings
Blakes print run of 2,168 set next to the base sale and a PSA 10 sale

unique: Dated completed-sale table matched to the pictured card, including logo foil, base, and Sapphire titles
Joyce Edwards Topps address ending in card-81, while SportsCardsPro #80 has zero sold listings so the $4.99 guide is left out
Mikayla Blakes Bowman U Now print run of 2,168 next to the June 18, 2026 base sale at $3.99
unverified: The source HTML did not arrive with the assignment, so the sentences were rebuilt from the fact-check and the linked pages. Ryan should read the wording before it is published.
The Watkins hero is a PSA 10 slab from a SportsCardsPro listing image. The cert number on that slab was not read off the photo. PSA cert 122909733 is the same card and grade.
A PSA population page was not opened, so no pop count is used.
Jazzy Davidson and Raven Johnson have no dated card sale in this draft.
Mikayla Blakes' full 2025-26 scoring average was not re-opened, so it is not quoted.
A $1.99 Mikaylah Williams sale on Aug. 1, 2026 was not on the Sapphire #4 sold list. The row used is Aug. 27, 2026 at $1.65.
An AP or USBWA second-team line for Joyce Edwards was not re-checked. The article uses the school bio and the WBCA coaches' list.

categories.name: Accuracy
categories.reason: Sales, awards, and season lines in the article were read from the linked pages. Unchecked lines were left out.

categories.name: Information gain
categories.reason: The sale table separates base cards from serials and foils, and it drops the Edwards guide price because that page has no completed sale.

categories.name: Effort and replication cost
categories.reason: Each pictured card was matched to a SportsCardsPro sold row, with the listing title and date kept.

categories.name: Originality
categories.reason: The ranking is a collecting cut, and the card-81 versus #80 note is specific to this draft.

categories.name: Experience and expertise
categories.reason: The intro links Ryan's public Angel Reese card collection. The sentences were rebuilt because the source HTML did not arrive.

categories.name: Main content and layout
categories.reason: The title is above the fold, the quick board sits under the intro, and the how-made note is at the bottom.

categories.name: Transparency
categories.reason: Every sale names SportsCardsPro and a date. The how-made note says Ryan wrote it and AI was used for fact-checking and formatting.

categories.name: Writing craft
categories.reason: Sentences stay on one card, one sale, and one award. The closing tells a reader what to do with the table.

categories.name: People-first purpose
categories.reason: A collector can compare the pictured card with a dated sale and skip a guide price that has no buyer.

categories.name: Human voice
categories.reason: The risk lines use a different label on each player, and the contrast constructions from the scorecard were rewritten in plain sentences.
